title: Donor Network Design Explorations
description:
Nicole sent notes on the donor recognition page — chiefly that it should not be called a wall, that it is "a network of nodes on a power grid," five candidate names, and milestone animations at 50/100/150/200. This session turned that into a shareable review deck at /donor-network.html: nine directions, each a designed graphic in which the 200 supporters MAKE the artwork rather than being plotted on top of one. Seven are network readings (power grid at night, supporters spelling POWER, a woven circle, one thickening ribbon, an overlapping bloom, a halftone numeral that draws the live count, concentric ripples) and two are deliberate off-brief controls with no graph at all, so the value of the node metaphor is actually tested rather than assumed. Every direction carries live search-and-focus, the four milestone animations, the four data states including the day-one empty view, and a downloadable 1080px supporter card. Each card takes a 1-10 rating and a comment, and one button exports all feedback as a text file — deliberately low-tech, because a published artifact cannot post anywhere and a review that needs a backend stops working the moment the link outlives the server.

Three things the note forced into the open, surfaced on the page itself as open questions rather than silently decided. First, the existing donor wall is organised entirely by giving level (groupDonorsByTier, DonorTierBand, DonorTierChips), but Nicole's bi-weekly spreadsheet carries no dollar amounts — so tiers have no input and founding-vs-supporter becomes the only distinction. Second, school and graduation year are the only structure the upload offers and are not on DonorLike at all. Third, and most consequential: the live site's anonymity contract withholds a donor's name, photo, link and initials together, and both a search box and a shareable card are new ways to undo that. The decision taken here is that an anonymous supporter is a visible node that counts toward every total and every milestone — withholding the node would make the wall quietly undercount people who asked only not to be named — but cannot be looked up and gets no card.

The pure rules live in src/lib/donorNetwork.js with 21 tests, not beside the exploration, because vitest's include is src/**: a module parked in .codeyam/ is one no test can reach. build.py inlines that same file into the page, so the anonymity rule has one copy rather than two that can quietly disagree.

Four real defects were found and fixed during the build, three of them silent. The milestone animation Nicole explicitly asked for was almost entirely broken: the growth step accelerates with the count, and the check required landing exactly on 50/100/150/200, so only the clamped 200 ever fired — milestoneCrossed now snaps to any milestone stepped over, and a test pins it. Every per-edge stroke weight was being discarded, because engine.css carries a `.edge { stroke-width: 1 }` default and a CSS rule outranks an SVG presentation attribute, so no taper or ribbon growth had ever actually rendered. build.py reported success while emitting a page that would have thrown on load, having not yet been told to inline the new rules module. And the timeline direction argued for momentum with a chart that was flat by construction, because gifts were spread evenly across the year.
